subject: Request: PrivateLink latency handback for Thermion (SLA note)
messages:
From: Maya Reyes <maya@thermion.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PrivateLink latency observations and request

Hi Chloe —

We noticed recurring tail latency spikes for inference requests that traverse our PrivateLink to Redwood. Typical user-visible times are fine, but during certain bursts our SLO dashboards show 200–400ms additional tail latency (95th–99th). Our networking team captured packet-level traces and some application-side timings and attached them (thermion_network_traces_20280409.zip).

Thermion runs an active edge appliance (customer-managed) in our colo that terminates TLS and peers to Redwood via PrivateLink. We believe much of the variability is introduced in our edge layer (deep packet inspection + reassembly under load). Given this, we want to propose a contract-level mechanism that 'hands back' responsibility for these specific latency tail events to Thermion (i.e., exclude them from Redwood's latency attribution) when they can be traced to customer-managed network appliances.

What we'd like:
- A short amendment to the Private deployment SLA that specifies an attribution test and a threshold (we were thinking 99th pct TCP RTT delta > X ms attributable to customer infra).
- A lightweight operational playbook for evidence collection so outages/latency incidents can be triaged without back-and-forth.

Can Redwood review the traces and tell us whether this is something you can accept as a carve-in to Thermion responsibility? Happy to set up time this week.

Thanks,
Maya
Head of Infrastructure, Thermion AI

--
Attachment: thermion_network_traces_20280409.zip (pcap, timing logs)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Maya Reyes <maya@thermion.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T11:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivateLink latency observations and request

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the traces and the clear ask. We can absolutely review and investigate. A few quick clarifying points before we dig in:

- Can you confirm whether the PrivateLink traffic is terminating at a Thermion-managed NLB in front of your edge appliance, or if the appliance is acting as the PrivateLink endpoint? That affects attribution.
- Do you have a reproducible window (time-of-day / load pattern) where the spikes are most frequent?
- Are you seeing any correlation with key rotation / TLS renegotiation events?

Operationally, Redwood's Private deployment contracts typically include a shared-responsibility section that attributes network-layer tail latency to customer-managed infrastructure when evidence shows packet-level queuing or appliance-induced reassembly. We also have a standard evidence checklist we can run through (pcap, per-hop RTT, server-side token timestamps).

I'll loop in Aditya and Laura to align on the commercial treatment and Priyom to validate the technical triage. Can you make 30 minutes available tomorrow (04/11) at 10:00 PT for a quick session?

—Chloe
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

--

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Maya Reyes <maya@thermion.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivateLink latency observations and request

Maya —

Appreciate the detail. From a commercial angle we can offer a targeted amendment that defines an attribution test and thresholds and adds an evidence protocol; we sometimes call this a "handback" clause for customer-managed network conditions. I attached a brief draft amendment that uses a percentile-based attribution (proposed 95th and an escalated 99th for severe events) and an evidence checklist — see proposed-handback-amendment-redwood-thermion.pdf.

Two negotiation points to flag up-front:
1) Metric choice — 95th is typical for production latency SLOs (and easier to operationalize), but customers often ask for 99th for tail protection. 99th is acceptable but will reduce the scope of Redwood's protection and therefore we treat it as a higher bar (we'd want a clearer evidence burden).
2) Caching and KV/HTTP optimizations — Redwood's runtime can reduce observed latencies via prefix caching and KV reuse; we will still accept handback for network-only factors, but where replayed cached responses reduce server CPU time on our side we expect both parties to account for that in the evidence.

If you're ok, Chloe/Laura and I can run the draft by your legal ops and iterate.

—Aditya
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: proposed-handback-amendment-redwood-thermion.pdf

From: Maya Reyes <maya@thermion.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Thermion NetOps <netops@thermion.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivateLink latency observations and request

Thanks, Aditya and Chloe —

Quick responses:
- Our endpoint is an appliance sitting behind a Thermion NLB; the appliance does TLS termination and performs content inspection.
- Spikes are most reproducible during 02:00–04:00 PT workloads and during batch inference spikes when a small subset of customers send long sequences.

We reviewed your draft and we have two asks:
1) Move the attribution threshold to 99th percentile (we want protection at the tail).
2) Explicitly exclude Redwood-side caching benefits from attribution — if a cached response reduces server time, that does not automatically make the spike "our" problem.

We attached two additional captures focusing on the 03:12–03:18 window (thermion_network_traces_20280411_additional.pcap inside the zip). Please have Priyom look at the SYN/ACK timing vs. Redwood token timestamps.

Happy to discuss on the call.

—Maya

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Maya Reyes <maya@thermion.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivateLink latency observations and request

Hi all —

Quick technical read of the artifacts: good captures, thank you. A few notes from the runtime perspective that will help separate responsibilities:

- KV cache / prefix cache effects: cached responses return with a much smaller server-side compute time; if your traces show that server token timestamps are still high, that points to server CPU or model queueing rather than network. In the traces you provided I see several spikes where the TCP RTT increases by ~250ms while server timestamps are flat — that pattern is consistent with customer-side queuing.
- TLS termination variance: because you terminate TLS on-prem, any TLS renegotiation or CRL checks that block the appliance will show up as network-side latency. We can instrument tracepoints on our side (we have a probe script) but we need synchronized clocks.
- Percentile choice: 99th is doable, but operationally it's noisier. If Thermion wants 99th we recommend a combined approach: 99th for hard handback when packet-level evidence exists, and a 95th advisory band where both parties investigate.

I've attached a simple probe script and a short test plan we ask customers to run (probe-scripts-testplan.tar.gz). If Thermion can run the script during your 02:00–04:00 window and share the results, we'll correlate them with our server-side logs.

—Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: probe-scripts-testplan.tar.gz

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Maya Reyes <maya@thermion.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivateLink latency observations and request

Maya —

Thanks for the thorough responses and for running the additional captures. Based on Priyom's analysis and our commercial review we've put together a short mutual action plan and a proposed SLA paragraph that tries to balance your request for tail protection with Redwood's need for a reproducible evidence bar. I've attached the proposed amendment and a one-page MAP that lays out steps, owners and timelines (signed-amendment-draft.docx).

Summary of the proposal (high level):
- Evidence bar: 99th percentile handback will be supported where packet-level captures align with a delta in TCP RTT >= 150ms and server-side timestamps show no corresponding model compute increase.
- Advisory band: 95th–99th will be a joint-investigation window where both parties run the probe script and agree on mitigations (e.g., adjust TLS session caching, reduce appliance inspection depth).
- Operational playbook: a short checklist for what to capture, where to put logs, and a 24-hour triage SLA for incidents that claim handback.
- Trial: a 30-day trial window during which Thermion runs the probe script daily during your 02:00–04:00 window. Redwood will correlate and produce weekly reports.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached documents and confirm you can run the probe script on 04/13 (we propose starting 04/13–05/12 trial).
2) If you're comfortable, we'll route the amendment through Legal Ops and propose a short DocuSign for signature.
3) Book a 30-minute kickoff for 04/14 10:00 PT — I included a calendar hold in the DocuSign link if you want to review the amendment synchronously.

If Thermion signs off, this gives both sides a clear evidentiary path so we don't have repeated finger-pointing on latency.

Regards,
Chloe
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

--
